doc.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022

title: Bernard Heiden and the Bartok sonata
summary: Studying Bartok in Heiden's arranging class, the music looked fantastic but sounded like garbage men.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Yeah. You just reminded me of something. I took arranging in college from Bernard Heiden. Do you recall him? Composer? He was at IU. Anyhow we had several classes, two semesters of it, and he got to talking and analyzing the Bartok Fourth Violin Sonata I guess it was. Okay. So as soon as class was over I ran up to the IU library and got the record out, put the headphones on — well we had a book. It was in the book. You had to buy the book, the score. And the way it was — the twelve tone — this way and this crest over here and down below this and the next page it was going this way and it came down and passed — I thought visually and intellectually hearing him talk about it and describe it, it was fantastic. And I knew this was going to be better than listening to Charlie Parker. So I went to the record and listened to it. It sounded — and I still think this today about my experience then, I played it two or three times, watching. It sounded like about four garbage men emptying the garbage. I didn’t know what to think. Because my eyes and my intellect told me this was a fantastic piece of work and for someone to write it out and then have it played, they must be great, and it must sound good. Boy it didn’t sound good to my ears. Not then anyway. Yeah so what you just read, I don’t know what to think. I don’t know.
